q25040.en: The policy limits (massimali) of the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance are the maximum amounts that the insurance company promises to pay in case of an accident.

explain.short: This is exactly what 'massimali' means: the top amount the insurer will pay for damage in an accident.
explain.rule: The 'massimali' (policy limits) are the maximum amounts the insurer pays for an accident. The law fixes the minimum; you can buy higher limits with a higher premium.
explain.trap: 'importi massimi' (maximum amounts) is the correct definition of 'massimali'.

sceneParams.caption: Massimali = the most the insurer will pay
lines: Accident: insurer pays for the damage

q25041.en: The minimum amount of the policy limits of the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance is set by law.

explain.short: The law fixes the lowest policy limits that every RCA policy must have, so victims are always protected.
explain.rule: The 'massimali' (policy limits) are the maximum amounts the insurer pays for an accident. The law fixes the minimum; you can buy higher limits with a higher premium.
explain.trap: 'cifra minima' (minimum amount): the law sets the minimum, the customer can go higher.

sceneParams.caption: The law sets the minimum policy limits
lines: The law sets the minimum limits
Every RCA policy must reach them

q25042.en: The policy limits of the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance can be increased, if the customer chooses, by paying a larger sum of money (insurance premium).

explain.short: Above the legal minimum you can choose higher limits. You get more protection, but the premium (the price) is higher.
explain.rule: The 'massimali' (policy limits) are the maximum amounts the insurer pays for an accident. The law fixes the minimum; you can buy higher limits with a higher premium.
explain.trap: 'a scelta del cliente' (if the customer chooses): higher limits are optional and cost more.

sceneParams.caption: Higher limits: your choice, higher price
lines: Want more? Pay a higher premium

q25043.en: The policy limits of the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance are the sums of money that the insurance company collects every year from its customer.

explain.short: The money you pay every year is the premium. The massimali are what the insurer pays OUT for an accident.
explain.rule: The 'massimali' (policy limits) are the maximum amounts the insurer pays for an accident. The law fixes the minimum; you can buy higher limits with a higher premium.
explain.trap: 'riscuote ogni anno' (collects every year) describes the premium, not the 'massimali'.

sceneParams.caption: You pay the premium; the insurer pays up to the limit
lines: You pay each year: the premium
Insurer pays for accidents: up to the limit

q25044.en: The policy limits of the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance increase every year.

explain.short: The limits stay as written in the contract. They change only if the customer chooses higher ones (and pays more) or if the law changes the minimum.
explain.rule: The 'massimali' (policy limits) are the maximum amounts the insurer pays for an accident. The law fixes the minimum; you can buy higher limits with a higher premium.
explain.trap: 'aumentano ogni anno' (increase every year): nothing increases by itself.

sceneParams.caption: Limits do not grow by themselves each year
lines: Limits are written in the contract
Higher only if you choose and pay

q25045.en: The policy limits of the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance are given back to the customer at the end of the year if no accidents are caused.

explain.short: The massimali are not money you deposit. They are only the maximum the insurer would pay, so nothing is given back.
explain.rule: The 'massimali' (policy limits) are the maximum amounts the insurer pays for an accident. The law fixes the minimum; you can buy higher limits with a higher premium.
explain.trap: 'vengono restituiti' (are given back): no money comes back to you; no accidents only means a lower premium with 'bonus malus'.

sceneParams.caption: Massimali are never given back to you
lines: No accidents: no refund of the limits

q25046.en: In RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance, the contract with the 'bonus malus' formula means the premium changes every year, based on the number of accidents caused.

explain.short: That is how 'bonus malus' works: a 'bonus' (lower price) if you cause no accidents, a 'malus' (higher price) if you cause them.
explain.rule: With 'bonus malus' the premium changes every year: it goes down if you cause no accidents and up if you cause them.
explain.trap: 'variazione annuale' (yearly change) 'in base al numero di incidenti causati' is the correct definition.

sceneParams.caption: Bonus malus: price changes with your accidents

q25047.en: The 'bonus malus' insurance formula does not apply to motorcycles.

explain.short: Bonus malus is used for motorcycles too, not only for cars.
explain.rule: With 'bonus malus' the premium changes every year: it goes down if you cause no accidents and up if you cause them.
explain.trap: 'non si applica per i motocicli' (does not apply to motorcycles) is wrong: motorcycles have it too.

sceneParams.caption: Bonus malus applies to motorcycles too

q25048.en: In RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance, the contract with the 'bonus malus' formula is automatically cancelled if you cause more than two accidents.

explain.short: Accidents do not cancel the contract. They only move you to a worse class, so the premium goes up.
explain.rule: With 'bonus malus' the premium changes every year: it goes down if you cause no accidents and up if you cause them.
explain.trap: 'viene automaticamente annullato' (is automatically cancelled): no, the price simply goes up.

sceneParams.caption: Accidents raise the price, they don't cancel it

q25049.en: In RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance, the contract with the 'bonus malus' formula is decided by a judge.

explain.short: A bonus malus contract is an agreement between the customer and the insurance company. No judge decides it.
explain.rule: With 'bonus malus' the premium changes every year: it goes down if you cause no accidents and up if you cause them.
explain.trap: 'stabilito dal giudice' (decided by a judge): a judge has nothing to do with it.

sceneParams.caption: Customer and insurer sign it, not a judge
lines: Customer and insurer sign the contract

q25050.en: RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance is valid also for accidents that happen in the countries of the European Union.

explain.short: Your Italian RCA also protects you when you drive in the other EU countries.
explain.rule: RCA pays for damage your vehicle causes to other people and their things, up to the policy limits. It does not cover crimes or fines.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also): valid in Italy AND in the EU countries.

sceneParams.caption: RCA is valid in the EU countries too
lines: And in the European Union countries

q25051.en: RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance also covers criminal liability, depending on the premium paid.

explain.short: RCA covers only CIVIL liability: paying for damage. Criminal liability (for crimes like injuring someone) is personal and no insurance can take it over.
explain.rule: RCA pays for damage your vehicle causes to other people and their things, up to the policy limits. It does not cover crimes or fines.
explain.trap: 'responsabilità penale' (criminal liability) is never covered, whatever premium you pay.

sceneParams.caption: RCA pays damage; crimes stay with the driver
lines: Civil liability: RCA pays the damage

q25052.en: RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance also covers the administrative fines provided by the Highway Code.

explain.short: Fines are the driver's own penalty for breaking the rules. RCA pays for damage to others, not your fines.
explain.rule: RCA pays for damage your vehicle causes to other people and their things, up to the policy limits. It does not cover crimes or fines.
explain.trap: 'sanzioni amministrative pecuniarie' (fines): you always pay them yourself.

sceneParams.caption: RCA does not pay your fines

q25053.en: RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance covers every damage caused, even if it is higher than the policy limit set.

explain.short: The insurer pays only up to the massimale (policy limit). Anything above it must be paid by whoever is responsible.
explain.rule: RCA pays for damage your vehicle causes to other people and their things, up to the policy limits. It does not cover crimes or fines.
explain.trap: 'anche se superiore al massimale' (even if higher than the limit): the limit is the maximum.

sceneParams.caption: RCA pays only up to the policy limit
lines: Insurer pays up to the limit
Above the limit: the responsible pays

q25054.en: RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance covers only the driver's liability, but not the liability of the owner of the vehicle.

explain.short: RCA covers the vehicle: the liability of the driver AND of the owner (who answers together with the driver).
explain.rule: RCA pays for damage your vehicle causes to other people and their things, up to the policy limits. It does not cover crimes or fines.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: both the driver and the owner are covered.

sceneParams.caption: RCA covers both the driver and the owner

q25055.en: RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance covers only damage caused to people, because damage to things needs another type of contract.

explain.short: RCA covers damage to other people AND to their things (for example another car or a wall).
explain.rule: RCA pays for damage your vehicle causes to other people and their things, up to the policy limits. It does not cover crimes or fines.
explain.trap: 'solo i danni arrecati alle persone' (only damage to people): things are covered too.

sceneParams.caption: RCA covers people AND things

keywords.it: solo i danni arrecati alle persone

q25057.en: After signing the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance contract, the insurance company must give the customer the insurance certificate.

explain.short: The insurance certificate proves the vehicle is insured. The insurer must give it to you after you sign.
explain.rule: RCA is compulsory by law. The insurer gives you the insurance certificate, which you keep on board. It covers damage whoever drives.
explain.trap: 'certificato di assicurazione' (insurance certificate) is the one document the insurer must give.

sceneParams.caption: The insurer gives you the insurance certificate

q25059.en: RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance is compulsory by law.

explain.short: Every vehicle on public roads must have RCA insurance. Without it you get a fine and the vehicle can be seized.
explain.rule: RCA is compulsory by law. The insurer gives you the insurance certificate, which you keep on board. It covers damage whoever drives.
explain.trap: 'obbligatoria per legge' (compulsory by law) is correct: it is not optional.

sceneParams.caption: RCA is compulsory by law
lines: Every vehicle on the road: RCA

q25060.en: The compulsory insurance certificate must always be kept on board the vehicle.

explain.short: The certificate is one of the documents the driver must carry, to show it to the police if asked.
explain.rule: RCA is compulsory by law. The insurer gives you the insurance certificate, which you keep on board. It covers damage whoever drives.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is correct here: the certificate is always kept on board.

sceneParams.caption: Keep the insurance certificate on board
lines: Show it at a police check

q25060.reviewNote: Since 2015 the windscreen sticker is gone and police check insurance electronically; official answer TRUE (art. 180 still lists the certificate).

q25061.en: After signing the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance contract, the insurance company must give the customer a list of partner body shops to contact in case of an accident.

explain.short: The only document the insurer must give is the insurance certificate. A list of body shops is not required.
explain.rule: RCA is compulsory by law. The insurer gives you the insurance certificate, which you keep on board. It covers damage whoever drives.
explain.trap: 'elenco delle autocarrozzerie' (list of body shops): not a required document.

sceneParams.caption: Required: the certificate, not a body shop list

q25062.en: After signing the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance contract, the insurance company must give the customer a booklet on first aid.

explain.short: The insurer must give the insurance certificate. A first aid booklet is not part of the contract.
explain.rule: RCA is compulsory by law. The insurer gives you the insurance certificate, which you keep on board. It covers damage whoever drives.
explain.trap: 'libretto sulle nozioni di pronto soccorso' (first aid booklet): not required.

sceneParams.caption: Required: the certificate, not a first aid book

q25063.en: After signing the RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance contract, the insurance company must give the customer a manual on how to avoid accidents.

explain.short: The insurer must give the insurance certificate. A safety manual is not required.
explain.rule: RCA is compulsory by law. The insurer gives you the insurance certificate, which you keep on board. It covers damage whoever drives.
explain.trap: 'manuale su come evitare incidenti' (manual on avoiding accidents): not required.

sceneParams.caption: Required: the certificate, not a safety manual

q25064.en: RCA (motor third-party liability) insurance, compulsory by law, includes compensation for damage caused by the vehicle, provided that it is driven by the owner.

explain.short: RCA covers damage caused by the vehicle whoever is driving it: the owner, a family member or a friend.
explain.rule: RCA is compulsory by law. The insurer gives you the insurance certificate, which you keep on board. It covers damage whoever drives.
explain.trap: 'purché guidato dal proprietario' (provided that the owner drives) is the false condition.

sceneParams.caption: RCA covers the vehicle, whoever drives

keywords.en: provided that it is driven by the owner

q31011.en: Being distracted while driving can cause road accidents that can have serious consequences.

explain.short: A moment of distraction is enough to miss a danger. The accident that follows can injure or kill people.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'può causare' (can cause) is true: distraction is a real accident risk.

sceneParams.caption: Distraction can cause serious accidents
lines: Eyes and mind on the road

q31012.en: When crossing a junction, you must keep maximum concentration while driving.

explain.short: Junctions are where many paths cross: cars, bikes and pedestrians. You need full concentration there.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'massima concentrazione' (maximum concentration) is right at a junction.

sceneParams.caption: Junction: maximum concentration

q31013.en: While driving, it is dangerous to take your eyes off the road, even for a few milliseconds.

explain.short: Even a very short look away means you travel some metres blind. A danger can appear in that moment.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'anche per pochi millisecondi' (even for a few milliseconds): even a tiny look away is a risk.

sceneParams.caption: Eyes off the road = driving blind
lines: Look away: the car keeps moving

q31014.en: To prevent the risk of accidents, the driver must carefully assess the behaviour of other road users.

explain.short: Watching others lets you predict their mistakes and react in time.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'valutare attentamente' (carefully assess) others is good defensive driving.

sceneParams.caption: Watch others and predict their moves

q31015.en: While driving, the perception of a danger and the driver's reaction to it are influenced by the environmental conditions.

explain.short: Rain, fog, night or glare make it harder to see a danger, so you notice it later and react later.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'sono influenzate' (are influenced) is true: weather and light change what you see.

sceneParams.caption: Weather and light change your reaction
lines: Fog, rain, night: you see less

q31016.en: Anxiety can reduce the ability to pay attention to dangers.

explain.short: An anxious mind is busy with worries, so it notices dangers less well.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'può ridurre' (can reduce) is true: anxiety steals attention.

sceneParams.caption: Anxiety reduces attention

q31017.en: A driver must keep in mind that he is not always able to judge his own driving abilities correctly.

explain.short: Many drivers think they drive better than they really do. Knowing this keeps you careful.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'non sempre' (not always) is true: we often overestimate ourselves.

sceneParams.caption: We often overrate our own driving

q31018.en: When driving, the ability to pay attention can also be affected by listening to music at a very high volume.

explain.short: Very loud music covers sounds like horns and sirens and takes part of your attention.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'volume molto alto' (very high volume) is the problem, not music itself.

sceneParams.caption: Loud music: you miss horns and sirens

keywords.en: music at a very high volume

q31019.en: Talking heatedly with other people on board the vehicle can have a negative effect on driving behaviour.

explain.short: An angry discussion takes your mind off the road and can make you drive nervously.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'animosamente' (heatedly) is the key: a heated talk distracts and upsets you.

sceneParams.caption: Heated arguments distract the driver
lines: Mind off the road, nervous driving

q31020.en: If you are not sure you can cross a junction in complete safety, you must stop and wait for all the vehicles that could collide with you to pass.

explain.short: When in doubt at a junction, stopping is always the safe choice.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'se non si è certi' (if you are not sure): then stop and wait.

sceneParams.caption: Not sure at a junction? Stop and wait

q31021.en: Passengers making a racket on board the vehicle can affect the driver's concentration.

explain.short: Noise and shouting inside the car take the driver's attention away from the road.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'schiamazzano' (make a racket) means shout and make noise: it distracts.

sceneParams.caption: Noisy passengers distract the driver

q31022.en: While driving, the driver must pay attention both to the road users in front of his vehicle and to those at the sides of the road.

explain.short: Dangers can come from ahead and from the sides, like a pedestrian stepping off the pavement.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'sia ... sia' (both ... and): watch ahead AND the sides.

sceneParams.caption: Watch ahead and the roadsides
lines: And the sides of the road

keywords.en: at the sides of the road

q31023.en: Concentrating on the satnav's directions can be a source of distraction while driving.

explain.short: If you focus on the satnav, your eyes and mind leave the road.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'può rappresentare' (can be) a distraction: true.

sceneParams.caption: Watching the satnav distracts

q31024.en: The driver must never overestimate his own driving skill.

explain.short: Overconfident drivers take bigger risks, like going too fast or overtaking badly.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'mai' (never) is right here: never overestimate yourself.

sceneParams.caption: Never overestimate your skill

q31025.en: Traffic rules are set to guarantee greater driving safety for all road users.

explain.short: The rules exist to protect everyone on the road: drivers, cyclists and pedestrians.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'per tutti gli utenti' (for all users): the rules protect everyone.

sceneParams.caption: Rules make the road safer for all

q31026.en: Respecting the traffic rules limits the risks of driving all vehicles, both motor vehicles and vehicles without a motor.

explain.short: Rules reduce risk for every vehicle: cars, motorbikes and also bicycles.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'sia ... sia' (both ... and): motor and non-motor vehicles alike.

sceneParams.caption: Rules cut risk for cars and bikes
lines: Less risk: cars and bikes too

q31027.en: Respecting the rules limits obstruction to traffic.

explain.short: When everyone follows the rules, traffic flows better and nobody blocks the others.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'intralcio' (obstruction) is reduced by following the rules: true.

sceneParams.caption: Rules keep traffic flowing

q31028.en: Using a mobile phone while driving is dangerous because it reduces attention to the road.

explain.short: A phone takes your eyes, hands and mind away from driving.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'riduce l'attenzione' (reduces attention) is the true reason.

sceneParams.caption: Phone at the wheel: less attention

q31029.en: Using a mobile phone while driving, even with a hands-free kit, can reduce attention to the road.

explain.short: Hands-free is allowed, but the conversation still takes part of your mind away from the road.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'anche se con impianto viva-voce' (even hands-free): the mind is still distracted.

sceneParams.caption: Hands-free still distracts your mind
lines: But the mind is on the call

q31030.en: Distraction while driving is one of the main causes of road accidents.

explain.short: Many accidents happen because the driver was looking at or thinking about something else.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'una delle principali cause' (one of the main causes): true.

sceneParams.caption: Distraction: a main cause of accidents
lines: One of the main accident causes

q31031.en: Attention while driving decreases when you are tired.

explain.short: A tired driver reacts more slowly and can even fall asleep. Stop and rest.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'affaticati' (tired): tiredness always lowers attention.

sceneParams.caption: Tired? Attention drops: take a break

q31032.en: Setting the satnav while driving reduces attention to the road.

explain.short: Typing an address needs your eyes and hands. Set the satnav before you leave or after stopping.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'mentre si guida' (while driving) is the problem: set it while stopped.

sceneParams.caption: Set the satnav before you leave

q31033.en: You can 'train' your attention while driving.

explain.short: With practice and good habits you learn where to look and how to spot dangers early.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'allenare' (train) is possible: attention improves with practice.

sceneParams.caption: Attention can be trained

q31034.en: Our senses cannot catch all the stimuli present in the environment.

explain.short: Our eyes and ears are limited: some things are too small, far, quick or hidden to notice.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'non riescono' (cannot): our senses have limits.

sceneParams.caption: Our senses miss some things

explain.short: Anger, joy, fear or sadness pull your thoughts away from the road.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'influenzano' (affect) is true: emotions change attention.

sceneParams.caption: Emotions change attention

q31036.en: Sometimes we expose ourselves to situations more risky than those we are able to handle.

explain.short: Drivers can take on more risk than their skills allow, for example speeding on a road they don't know.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'a volte' (sometimes) is true: it happens.

sceneParams.caption: We sometimes take more risk than we can handle

q31037.en: The driver may take his eyes off the road when he thinks there is no immediate danger of an accident.

explain.short: A danger can appear suddenly, exactly when you think the road is safe. Keep your eyes on the road.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'quando ritiene' (when he thinks): your opinion does not make it safe.

sceneParams.caption: Never look away, even if it seems safe
lines: 'No danger' can change in a second
Keep your eyes on the road

q31038.en: Near a junction a driver may stop and, while waiting for other vehicles to pass, may send a quick message with the mobile phone.

explain.short: Even when stopped at a junction you are still driving in traffic. You must be ready to move and watch everyone.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'rapido messaggio' (quick message): no message is quick enough at a junction.

sceneParams.caption: No texting while waiting at a junction
lines: Stopped at a junction: still driving

q31039.en: A driver who wants to go first at a junction must arrive at it faster.

explain.short: Speed does not give you priority. You must approach a junction slowly and respect the priority rules.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'più velocemente' (faster) is wrong: slow down at junctions.

sceneParams.caption: Approach junctions slowly, speed gives no priority

q31040.en: While driving, if the driver thinks there is no immediate danger, he can dial a phone number on the mobile phone without stopping.

explain.short: Dialling takes your eyes and hands off driving. Using a hand-held phone while driving is forbidden.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'qualora il conducente ritenga' (if the driver thinks): your opinion does not allow it.

sceneParams.caption: Never dial a number while driving

q31041.en: The behaviour of other road users makes no difference to safe driving.

explain.short: Other people's behaviour matters a lot: you must watch it and adapt to it.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'ininfluente' (makes no difference) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Others' behaviour matters for safety

q31042.en: The driver may ignore the behaviour of other road users if they do not respect the rules of the Highway Code.

explain.short: People who break the rules are the most dangerous: watch them even more closely.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'può non tenere conto' (may ignore): the opposite, pay more attention.

sceneParams.caption: Rule-breakers need MORE attention

q31043.en: While driving, the perception of a danger and the driver's reaction to it are not influenced by the environmental conditions.

explain.short: Fog, rain, darkness or glare do change how quickly you see a danger and react.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'non sono influenzate' (are not influenced): wrong, they are.

sceneParams.caption: Weather and light DO change your reaction
lines: Fog, rain, night: you see less

q31044.en: A driver must always underestimate dangerous situations so as not to be overwhelmed by anxiety while driving.

explain.short: Underestimating danger makes you careless. You must judge danger correctly and stay calm.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'sottostimare' (underestimate) is wrong: judge danger correctly.

sceneParams.caption: Judge danger correctly, don't play it down

q31045.en: The driver must accept the passengers' requests to drive faster.

explain.short: The driver decides the speed, based on the rules and the conditions, not on passengers.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'deve accogliere' (must accept) is wrong: you are responsible, not them.

sceneParams.caption: You decide the speed, not the passengers

q31046.en: The driver must focus mainly on the stretch of road no more than three metres in front of his vehicle.

explain.short: Three metres is far too close. You must look far ahead, and also at the sides and in the mirrors.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'non superiore a tre metri' (no more than three metres) is wrong: look far ahead.

sceneParams.caption: Look far ahead, not just 3 metres

q31047.en: While the vehicle is moving, the driver can program the satnav at any time.

explain.short: Programming the satnav takes eyes and hands off driving. Do it before leaving or when stopped.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'in qualsiasi momento' (at any time): no, only when stopped.

sceneParams.caption: Program the satnav only when stopped
lines: Car moving: hands off the satnav

q31048.en: The rear-view mirror on the right side of the vehicle must be used only by expert drivers.

explain.short: Every driver must use all the mirrors, including the right one, to see what is around.
explain.rule: Watch all other road users and predict what they will do. At a junction, if you are not sure you can cross safely, stop and wait.
explain.trap: 'solo da conducenti esperti' (only by expert drivers) is wrong: everyone uses it.

sceneParams.caption: Every driver uses the right mirror

q31049.en: The rear-view mirrors must be adjusted while the vehicle is moving.

explain.short: Adjust the mirrors before you set off, with the car stopped. Doing it while moving distracts you.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'mentre il veicolo è in movimento' (while moving) is wrong: adjust them before leaving.

sceneParams.caption: Adjust mirrors before setting off

q31050.en: Respecting traffic rules is important only if breaking them leads to a high fine.

explain.short: Rules protect lives. You respect them always, whatever the fine.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'solo se' (only if) is the trap: the size of the fine does not matter.

sceneParams.caption: Respect every rule, whatever the fine

q31051.en: Respecting traffic rules is important for vulnerable road users, but not for drivers of motor vehicles.

explain.short: Rules apply to everyone. Car drivers must respect them too, also to protect pedestrians and cyclists.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'ma non per i conducenti' (but not for drivers) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Rules apply to drivers too

q31052.en: Respecting traffic rules is important when traffic is very heavy, but not when traffic is flowing freely.

explain.short: Rules apply in every traffic condition. Free-flowing roads bring their own risks, like high speed.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'ma non quando ... scorrevole' (but not when flowing freely) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Rules apply in light traffic too

q31053.en: A no-overtaking rule may be ignored if you have been queuing behind a slow vehicle for more than 10 minutes and you think you can overtake without danger.

explain.short: A no-overtaking ban must always be respected, however long you have been waiting.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'più di 10 minuti' (more than 10 minutes): waiting time never cancels a ban.

sceneParams.caption: No overtaking means no overtaking, always

q31054.en: Keeping your position on the carriageway is a secondary rule that, if needed, may not be respected.

explain.short: Keeping right in your lane is a basic safety rule. It avoids head-on crashes and must always be respected.
explain.rule: Traffic rules exist to make the road safer for everyone. Respect them always, in every situation, whatever the fine.
explain.trap: 'norma secondaria' (secondary rule) is wrong: it is a basic rule.

sceneParams.caption: Keep your position: a basic rule

q31055.en: Attention while driving is important only when doing dangerous manoeuvres, for example an overtake.

explain.short: You need attention all the time, also when driving straight on a quiet road.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: attention is needed always.

sceneParams.caption: Attention always, not only when overtaking

q31056.en: Drinking a strong liquor improves attention about 10 minutes after drinking it.

explain.short: Alcohol never improves attention. It slows reactions and makes you overconfident.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'permette di migliorare' (improves) is wrong: alcohol always makes attention worse.

sceneParams.caption: Alcohol never improves attention

q31057.en: Tuning the car radio by hand causes no loss of attention to the road, because it is a task you are used to doing.

explain.short: Even a familiar task takes your eyes and hands off driving for a moment. That is a loss of attention.
explain.rule: Driving needs full attention all the time. Anything that takes your eyes or mind off the road (phone, satnav, radio, passengers, emotions, tiredness, alcohol) raises the risk of an accident.
explain.trap: 'non comporta perdita di attenzione' (causes no loss of attention) is wrong: habit does not make it safe.

sceneParams.caption: Tuning the radio still distracts
lines: Hand on the radio, eyes on it

q31058.en: If you are slightly drunk, you can still drive safely.

explain.short: Even a little alcohol slows reactions and worsens judgement. You cannot drive safely.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'ebbrezza lieve' (slightly drunk): still not safe.

sceneParams.caption: Slightly drunk is still unsafe

q31059.en: The amount of attention you can give to the road while driving is unlimited.

explain.short: Attention is limited. If you give some to the phone or the radio, less is left for the road.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'illimitata' (unlimited) is wrong: attention is limited.

sceneParams.caption: Attention is limited
lines: Give it all to the road

q31060.en: With 0.5 grams per litre of alcohol in the blood you can concentrate better.

explain.short: Alcohol never improves concentration. Even at this level reactions and judgement get worse.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'si riesce a concentrarsi meglio' (you concentrate better) is wrong: alcohol makes it worse.

sceneParams.caption: Alcohol never helps concentration

q31061.en: Our senses can catch all the stimuli present in the environment.

explain.short: Our senses are limited: we always miss some things around us.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'tutti gli stimoli' (all the stimuli) is wrong: we cannot catch everything.

sceneParams.caption: Our senses cannot catch everything

q31062.en: Our senses are able to perceive stimuli of any intensity.

explain.short: Very weak stimuli (a faint sound, a dim light) can go unnoticed. Our senses have limits.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'di qualunque intensità' (of any intensity) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Weak signals can go unnoticed

q31063.en: In heavy traffic, stress can help the driver stay alert.

explain.short: Stress makes you nervous and less attentive. It does not help you drive.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'può aiutare' (can help) is wrong: stress worsens attention.

sceneParams.caption: Stress makes driving worse

q31064.en: Hearing is not an important sense when driving.

explain.short: Hearing warns you of horns, sirens and engines you cannot see yet.
explain.rule: Our senses and attention are limited. Emotions, anxiety, stress, tiredness and alcohol make them work worse, never better.
explain.trap: 'non è un senso importante' (is not important) is wrong: hearing matters.

sceneParams.caption: Hearing matters: horns and sirens
